_doc: Shrink-only disclosed list of enforcement claims that have NOT declared whether their gate has an exemption surface (GHI #797). Seeded 2026-08-12 at the population measured on main. An entry records a DISCLOSED absence of a declaration, never a justified one: acceptance means the count is visible and the per-claim ruling is still owed, not that the claim is fine undeclared. NEVER add an entry to silence a newly-authored claim -- declare it instead (exempts='none', or the claim id of the control that exercises the exemption); that is the laundering ADR-0.0.73 Boundary Invariant #8 forbids. An entry MUST be surrendered the moment its claim declares (gz validate --exemption-controls fails closed on a stale acceptance), which is what makes the list shrink-only. The 'reason' is UNIFORM across every entry because the fact is uniform: nobody has looked. A per-claim hint was attempted at the cutover and DROPPED -- it scanned each claim's EnforcementClaimRecord.source_file for an exemption-surface naming convention and matched 0 of 70, because source_file points at the negative-control shim in _qc_nc_entrypoints.py rather than at the gate the shim delegates to. A hint that measures the wrong file is decoration, and shipping it would have dressed 70 identical unknowns as 70 findings. Enforced by src/gzkit/governance/trust_audits/exemption_controls.py and ratcheted via data/waiver_ratchet_registry.json.

measurement.population_derivation: Every claim in the @enforces registry after _ensure_production_claims_registered(). The registry is the single authority for what an enforcement claim IS; re-deriving the population by scanning for decorators would be a second reader free to disagree with the first (.claude/rules/hexagonal-architecture.md rule 8).
measurement.note: Of the 13 declared claims, 5 are the exemplar gates seeded with the mechanism at the 2026-08-12 cutover: the verifier-pipe gate (GHI #796) and the handoff resume gate (GHI #795). Both had registered, enrolled, PASSING controls throughout the life of their exemption holes, which is the evidence this inventory exists on. The other 8 were surrendered on 2026-08-14 by the first triage pass (operator ruling: 'declare only the honest none's') -- each gate was read end-to-end, found to carry no admit path, and declared exempts='none' in _QC_CLAIM_EXEMPTS. That pass also read or located the admit path of ~46 of the remaining claims WITHOUT declaring them, because a gate with an exemption owes a control that exercises it and writing those is the enrollment the 2026-08-12 inventory-not-enrollment ruling declined. Read docs/governance/exemption-control-triage.md before the next drain: it records the bar applied, the per-claim admit paths already located, and the 17 claims not yet reached -- so the next pass starts from a reading rather than re-deriving one.

UNDECLARED, ruling owed. This gate's OWN exemption surface is the accepted_claims list in this file -- a claim on it is excused from the undeclared finding -- so by this gate's own rule it owes a control proving the list admits only a genuinely undeclared claim. The stale-acceptance and deleted-claim arms are covered by unit tests today; promoting one to a registered exemption control needs the _QC_NEGATIVE_CONTROL_TABLE to carry an exempts field, which is a separate change. Disclosed rather than silently exempted.
